Let <MATH_0001> be functors with right
adjoints <MATH_0002>. Let <MATH_0003>
be a transformation of functors. Let <MATH_0004> be
the corresponding transformation of adjoint functors. Then
<MATH_0005>
is commutative where the unlabeled arrows are the counit transformations.

$$
\Mor(u_1 v_1 D, D') \to \Mor(u_2 v_1 D, D')
$$

This is true because <MATH_0001> is the unique
morphism such that the induced maps <MATH_0002>
is the map <MATH_0003> induced by
<MATH_0004>. Namely, this means the map
<MATH_0005>
induced by <MATH_0006> is the same as the map
<MATH_0007>
induced by <MATH_0008>. Taking <MATH_0009> we find that the counit
<MATH_0010> precomposed by <MATH_0011> corresponds to <MATH_0012>
under adjunction. This exactly means that the diagram commutes when
evaluated on <MATH_0013>.
